PullRequest.Title: Show Chat view session actions in the shared sessions list menu
PullRequest.Body:
The session row context menu in editor windows is now the union of the old Chat view agent sessions menu and the shared sessions list menu.

- Registers Open as Editor, Open to the Side, Open in New Window, Open Customizations, Mark All as Read, Open Host Settings and Open Session Settings on the shared menu, gated to editor windows (the Agents window already has its own entries). Existing keybindings are unchanged; Pin, Mark as Unread, Mark as Done, Rename and Delete are not duplicated.
- Groups: navigation, 1_state, 4_manage, with Delete last.
- Adds an adapter so the actions run on the list's session rows.

How to test: right-click a session in the Sessions list of an editor window and check the items and order.

Tests: agentSessionsActions.test.ts (16 passing), typecheck-client, oxlint.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore an editor window and open a shared session-row context menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Registration adds a fixed number of action/menu descriptors. Right-click creates one context overlay and menu, evaluates conditions, and builds actions; none of the newly contributed command bodies runs before selection.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Seven added menu entries, independent of total session count. Existing selection processing scales with selected rows, unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous menu construction; no added asynchronous task, process, subscription, or I/O burst. The existing disposable store is cleared on menu dismissal or replacement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or eager service/model resolution. The adapter runs only on command execution. Existing menu construction and disposal apply equally on first and subsequent openings.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected every changed hunk and sessionsList.ts:9002-9140; menu.getActions constructs actions rather than executing them. Settings contribution registration already existed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Menu construction duration was not measured, but added work is a small fixed set of descriptors and conditions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no heavyweight work moves into startup or menu display, and no new retained per-opening resource lacks cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open selected shared-list sessions as editors, to the side, or in an auxiliary window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After explicit invocation, adapt selected resources, resolve agent sessions, then await each existing chatWidgetService.openSession call sequentially. A cold session must acquire/load its model before its chat editor is usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read local session data via _chatSessionStore.readSession when no model reference exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one local-session load request per selected cold session in the normal path; warm models return before the store read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Open actions already performed this work from the legacy Chat view; the shared list did not expose these entries. The diff adds a deliberate invocation route, not additional loads per open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold model loading is awaited by the requested editor opening; successive selections are opened serially.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve provider session content through getOrCreateChatSession and open the requested editor/auxiliary target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical provider load per distinct cold session resource, with concurrent same-resource remote loads coalesced by _remoteSessionLoads. Existing loaded models are reused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical provider loading, model ownership, editor reuse, and auxiliary-target behavior existed for these commands. Only the shared-menu route and resource adapter are added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider resolution and editor opening are awaited; existing remote history restoration remains on the same path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K selected known sessions. Adapter and existing context normalization perform up to two lookups per selected resource; top-level lookups use ResourceMap. Child/missing-resource lookups can scan parents. There is one requested editor open per surviving selection, not per session in history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing for/await loop opens one selected session at a time. Same-resource remote loads share an in-flight load; the diff introduces no global parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: getSession is an in-memory lookup and does not resolve providers. Unknown array entries are filtered without loading them. Existing model reuse and per-resource remote-load coalescing remain intact; no new cache or retry loop is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the adapter, BaseAgentSessionAction, BaseOpenAgentSessionAction, ChatWidgetService, ChatEditorInput.resolve, and model acquisition/loading. No duplicate boundary call is introduced by the second in-memory lookup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold history sizes, selected-row counts, provider latency, and auxiliary-window cost vary and were not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: this exposes existing user-requested operations without changing their boundary multiplicity, concurrency, or model lifetime.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Customizations for one shared-list session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An explicitly chosen action validates that exactly one row is selected, executes the existing OpenEditor command once, selects its session context, and opens the singleton customization editor. Migration discovery is launched without awaiting it in setInput.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the existing AICustomizationManagementEditorInput singleton for the selected session context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One executeCommand and one editorService.openEditor request per user invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The legacy Open Customizations command passed the same sessionResource and opened the same singleton editor. The shared list gains a separate enablement descriptor and uses the same helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Editor opening is awaited. No editor is opened while merely displaying the menu.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing migration discovery lists prompt files and requests migration/source-folder information from customization providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing category-level parallel work for one active session; source-folder requests are grouped by distinct target type. The diff does not add discovery passes or alter provider caching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same editor invoked through the legacy action performed the same background discovery. No discovery is added to menu creation or multiplied by the adapter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: setInput starts refreshCustomizationMigrationInfo with void; discovery does not block the action's editor-open completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one selected session. Existing background discovery scales with enabled migration categories, customization candidates, and distinct target types, not with all sessions or selected rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One action invocation for one session. Existing migration categories run with Promise.all, and superseded refresh requests are canceled/coalesced by the existing editor machinery.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The customization editor input is singleton getOrCreate. Existing refresh uses a zero-delay Delayer, cancellation, and sequence/context guards; the new helper introduces no cache or additional state retention. Provider-level cold/warm costs are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both actions call the same helper once; inspected command handling, editor setInput/clearInput, and migration scheduling/discovery.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Underlying customization inventories, provider cache hits, and discovery latency were not profiled; no changed multiplier or scheduling mechanism was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff changes availability and selection enablement, not the existing editor's expensive work or its scheduling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Mark all agent sessions as read from the shared-list menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Explicit selection invokes the existing action once, scans the existing model, filters nonarchived unread sessions, and synchronously submits their existing read-state mutations. Host echoes/persistence complete through existing services.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider-owned read state reaches the existing controller and host connection.dispatch(SessionIsReadChanged). Locally owned state updates the in-memory state map instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one host dispatch per unread provider-owned session, with unchanged read-state checks in model and store. Local state persistence remains deferred to onWillSaveState.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Mark All as Read action already scanned and mutated this collection from its legacy menu and command-palette entry. The new shared-menu descriptor does not change the loop, dispatch count, or event behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Submission occurs in the action loop; the action does not await a round trip for every session.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N model sessions are scanned, and U nonarchived unread sessions are mutated. Shared-list selected-row count does not multiply the command or the full-model scan.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous scan and mutation loop, not one command per selected row. Existing host dispatches are submitted without new await/parallelism changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The action reads the existing model rather than refreshing providers. Already-read and archived sessions are excluded; the host store also suppresses unchanged known flags. No new cache or failure retry behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the menu argument, unchanged action loop, model state handling, controller routing, and store dispatch/deduplication.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Unread-session counts and downstream provider responsiveness vary. Existing collection-wide behavior can be costly, but its mechanism predates this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: adding another explicit entry point does not independently establish a higher-frequency or higher-cardinality execution mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open local agent-host settings from a shared session row
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The gated menu item explicitly opens one pinned synthetic settings resource. Its filesystem provider serializes the existing cached root configuration; menu visibility itself performs no configuration fetch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serve a synthetic JSONC settings document by serializing cached root config and encoding bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing editor filesystem stat/read lifecycle for one fixed settings URI; no per-session enumeration or host request is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command already opened this resource from the legacy menu and command palette, using the same cached provider and serialization path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Document reads are on settings-editor opening, after explicit command selection, not on context-menu display.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One ambient host/settings URI, independent of how many sessions are selected. Serialization scales with the existing host configuration size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One openEditor call per invocation; no selection loop and no added parallel work. Existing file-watch disposal remains unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider caches ambient root config and listens to existing rootState changes. Repeated settings opens use the same resource/editor machinery. No new root subscription or provider registration is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected registration, command body, host settings cache, and abstract provider stat/read/watch ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Root configuration size and filesystem-service read counts were not measured; no change in their per-open cost was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: fixed-target user-requested access reuses an existing cache and provider without moving work to startup or menu rendering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open one local agent session's settings from the shared-list menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The single-selection-gated action converts the selected resource to backend identity and opens one synthetic session-settings URI. Existing provider stat/read/watch paths acquire managed references; incoming state updates refresh the document through existing events.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire a managed session-state subscription, subscribing across the host connection when no live entry exists; release operation-scoped references and retain watch-scoped references until disposal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Concurrent references for the same backend resource share one live subscription. A fresh acquisition after all references are released may subscribe again; failed entries are replaced on a later acquisition. All of these rules are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing session-settings action and filesystem provider performed the same operations for legacy Chat-view selections. The diff accepts a one-row array and adds its menu route, without adding acquisitions per stat/read/watch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing asynchronous subscription initialization can delay availability of populated settings state. The action does not fetch or subscribe while constructing the menu.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the managed session config to the synthetic JSONC document and encode it for the editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing document lifecycle for one selected resource, with no new per-property or per-session boundary fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical serialization occurred when opening the same settings URI through the previous context-menu action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs during settings document access after explicit selection; not during menu evaluation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one selected backend session per invocation. Config serialization scales with that session's configuration, not total sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-session action only. Existing overlapping filesystem operations coalesce at the live subscription entry; no selected-session subscription burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Identity resolution is synchronous. Subscription manager reuses live/pending same-resource entries and refcounts references; errors can be retried on reacquisition. stat/read release references in finally, and watch disposal releases its reference. No new cache keys or unbounded retention are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced array selection resolution, identity conversion, filesystem provider acquisition/release, and subscription manager reuse/error/release behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual cold subscription latency and filesystem lifecycle ordering were not measured; these pre-existing mechanisms are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: selection stays bounded to one session, and existing coalescing and cleanup remain intact.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all six changed files and all diff pages against base 3b381b139291d9bbdd5a5a1ae60d41dad26d137d. Traced menu construction and each newly exposed action's critical path, effective cardinality, caches, boundaries, concurrency, and disposal. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix was established. Static read-only review; no runtime measurements.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
